newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota small grain crops develop rapidly.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota small grain crops develop rapidly.

text.p: North Dakota's small grain crops developed rapidly and began turning color during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
But small grain development remained behind average, and rain and high humidity created concern about scab and midge emergence in wheat, the report said.

Spring wheat was 38 percent in the milk or beyond stage, against 19 last week, 33 last year and 42 percent on average. Spring wheat condition was rated 44 percent good to excellent, unchanged from 44 percent at that level last week.
Durum wheat was rated 35 percent good to excellent, against 28 percent at that level last week. Durum was 66 percent heading, against 51 last week, 65 last year and 67 percent on average.

Meanwhile, late-season crops made "excellent" progress and entered more advanced stages of development, mostly ahead of the average pace. Potatoes were 85 percent blooming, against 39 last week, 70 last year and 69 on average.
The state's topsoil moisture supplies increased slightly over the previous week and were rated 14 percent surplus, 69 adequate, 15 short and two very short.
